segments.text: When a core reaches ten million kelvin, hydrogen atoms begin the proton‑proton chain, releasing energy.
In stars just over one solar mass, the CNO cycle adds a large share of that power.
Hydrostatic equilibrium balances outward gas pressure with inward gravity, keeping the star stable.
The Sun sits on this balance, burning hydrogen for about ten billion years and is halfway through that span.
This steady fusion lets the star remain on the main‑sequence and stay a main‑sequence.
